recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if the Security WG wants a separate R6-era harmonization of agent reference targets and narrative, not to complete FHIR-30203 itself.
issue_request: FHIR-30203 was a Published FHIR-core Security change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking Provenance and AuditEvent narrative to clarify that an agent is broader than a person and can include teams, software, devices, organizations, care teams, and other responsible actors.
initial_application: Commit aa9defa3c842c9dfc93f512695904c954ddb1c7b added the requested AuditEvent paragraph and Provenance Agent wording to the source in April 2021. Later source maintenance preserved the clarification while applying broader QA and R6 security edits.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists Provenance and AuditEvent, confirming the inspected resource source is in build scope. Current Provenance narrative identifies responsibility by participation type and lists person, device, system, organization, group, care-team, or identifiable thing examples. Current AuditEvent narrative identifies the participating who as the agent and lists person, organization, software, device, or other responsible actors. Later FHIR-49672 concerns R6 agent reference-target types and does not reverse this R5 narrative clarification.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already conveys the approved FHIR-30203 clarification; minor wording/style differences such as MAY capitalization and might be versus may be do not change implementer understanding.
